query: How can we reduce declined travel expenses?

per_column.name: is_travel_declined
per_column.rationale: Binary encoding of the focus/outcome (declined travel expense), not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: amount_risk_level
per_column.rationale: Derived risk banding of the expense amount; amount plausibly drives both scrutiny/processing decisions and decline likelihood. It is a common cause rather than an intervenable lever. Not named in the query.

per_column.name: item_type
per_column.rationale: Type of item purchased affects both approval policy applicability and decline probability; it is an attribute, not something an actor sets to influence declines. Not named in query.

per_column.name: days_to_process
per_column.rationale: Processing turnaround is an operationally settable/changeable lever a team could intervene on; plausibly affects decline outcomes. Qualifies as an intervenable treatment, though it may partly be a mediator.

judge.rationale: The set does contain one plausibly intervenable treatment (days_to_process), satisfying part (a) weakly. However, the identified confounders (amount_risk_level, item_type) are not clearly common causes of processing time AND decline; they are more naturally attributes of the expense that predict decline, and their status as confounders of the treatment->outcome relation is weak. No clearly established confounder that jointly causes processing time and decline is provided. The columns are generic/derived features rather than a deliberate confounder-adjustment set for an interventional question, so the what-if claim is only partially realised.
